publication_search.result: No post-round-38 public PR, commit, default-branch code result, or matching branch carries a scope-less resume completeness journal/watermark.

fixed_source.fact: tool_index calls set_active_project for every request and passes None when changed_paths/removed_paths are absent.

set_active_project calls start_watcher; start_watcher replaces the tracked watcher and starts it only when auto_index.enabled is true. maybe_auto_index and scope-less manual builds call run_split_build with None.

RecommendedWatcher records changed/removed sets, treats folder/rename/unknown/incomplete-remove/error/rescan as rescan_needed, debounces staging into pending, and drains by destructive take. It exposes no durable cursor, delivery fence, or build-linked acknowledgement token.
run_split_build transports only Option<&BuildScope>; success has no journal acknowledgement and stale retry reuses the same scope.

phase_scan_and_diff only takes the targeted path for a nonempty BuildScope; scope-less and empty scopes execute scan_with_manifest. Scoped trust assumes the supplied events are the complete changes since the prior build.
prepare captures project inputs after scan/diff and commit guards index_epoch, but no filesystem observation generation is captured or acknowledged.

watcher_trait.fact: Watcher offers new, watch, unwatch, kind, paths_mut, and configure; it does not expose an event-delivery barrier or a filesystem mutation cursor.

rescan_flag.fact: Rescan indicates a lapse or state change that invalidates events, but is emitted only by some platforms/backends.

known_problems.fact: The library documents filesystems/platform cases that may emit no events or miss events; RecommendedWatcher alone is therefore not a cross-platform completeness proof.

reason: Keeping the present FileWatcher alive and reusing its changed/removed set would optimize only auto-index-enabled sessions and would still be reset by repeated tool_index set_active_project calls unless lifecycle changes are made.

Starting a RecommendedWatcher for auto_index=false removes one lifecycle gap but does not produce a complete delivery watermark. An empty queue is not proof that no undeclared filesystem change occurred.
Directory mtimes, root mtimes, git status, the durable dirty-closure state, and the SQLite index epoch each miss valid classes of source/config/infra changes. None can certify scope-less no-change.
A PollWatcher may rewalk/hash the tree, moving rather than removing the 100k scan cost; excluding that work from the measured build would be benchmark-accounting distortion.
Changing p8_scale to pass known changed_paths would alter the fixed scope-less protocol and is prohibited.

minimum_future_safe_slice.public_protocol: No MCP parameter change. tool_index remains scope-less.

internal_components.name: ProjectMutationObserver
internal_components.owner: ProjectServices, keyed by normalized project path
internal_components.lifetime: Created once with the project runtime, independent of auto_index; never replaced merely because the same project becomes active again.
internal_components.contract: begin/full-baseline/changes_since/ack, returning Complete, Overflow, Unready, Unsupported, or IdentityMismatch.

internal_components.name: ObservationToken
internal_components.rule: Only a Complete interval may authorize a targeted scan; every other result falls back to the current scan_with_manifest path.

internal_components.name: BuildObservationLease
internal_components.rule: Acquire under the existing per-project build gate; snapshot but do not destructively acknowledge events before prepare/commit. Ack the end token only after stage 3 succeeds. Failure, panic, stale retry exhaustion, close/reopen, or observer restart forces full reconciliation.

minimum_future_safe_slice.backend_requirement: At least one explicitly supported backend must supply a documented, testable complete cursor/fence. notify RecommendedWatcher callbacks alone do not meet this contract. Other platforms/filesystems stay on full scan until their backend supplies the same proof.
minimum_future_safe_slice.baseline_rule: First build after observer creation/restart/identity change remains a full scan. Observer coverage must begin before it; events accumulated during the full build are retained as conservative next-build work unless the backend can fence and prove them included.
minimum_future_safe_slice.scope_derivation: Complete empty interval yields a DB-universe no-files-changed ScanDiffResult and may continue only durable resolution work. Complete nonempty interval becomes the existing BuildScope path. Dot paths, directory/rename events, config/admission changes, >512 events, unsupported path encodings, overflow, and observer errors force full scan.
minimum_future_safe_slice.explainability: Record scan mode, start/end token identities, fallback reason, and acknowledgement outcome in BuildExplain without changing benchmark stages or treating diagnostics as acceptance.

required_negative_controls: undeclared source edit between successful scope-less builds
create, delete, rename, directory creation/removal, and replacement-save patterns
hidden config and infra files outside ordinary source admission
backend overflow/error, missing event, watcher restart, and project reactivation
project cache eviction, close/reopen, DB replacement, DB incarnation/index_epoch mismatch
prepare failure, stage-1 failure, stage-2 failure, stage-3 failure, and stale retry
B=200 unchanged, resume=1024 unchanged, same number and order of benchmark stages and reports
full-scan parity after every forced fallback
non_solutions: Do not cache WalkManifest as a freshness certificate.
Do not infer filesystem quiescence from resolution_freshness.complete.
Do not turn empty scope into no-op.
Do not use root/directory mtimes as a content-completeness proof.
Do not make the benchmark scoped or add a wider dirty budget to repair the fixed population.
Do not hide an equivalent full-tree poll outside measured build windows.
